name: Verification without provisioning: retire the throwaway-user path
result: COMPLETE in code, and the part that mattered SURVIVED a later deletion. The harness can no longer create a user, and that guarantee is asserted at the transport by test_run_never_creates_or_deletes_a_user. What did NOT survive is everything built to put the harness back on a six-hourly production schedule: PR #343 deleted the workflow, the CLI entrypoint and the RBAC_VERIFY_PRINCIPALS environment variable the same night, because the scheduled job was never asked for. RbacVerifier is now driven only by its tests, against a FastAPI TestClient with enforcement on. It needs no credential, no schedule and no production access. See corrected_at_sprint_close.
why: Commit 2703c6e disarmed the six-hourly schedule Sprint 55 had shipped ~90 minutes earlier, and named this fix without attempting it: scripts/rbac_verify.py::run() provisioned four real accounts via POST /admin/users using a password committed at line 74, minted API keys for them and purged them at the end. reconcile_throwaway_users() existed precisely because teardown leaks when a run is cancelled. On a cron that is a role-by-route ENFORCEMENT CHECK mutating the production auth table every six hours, forever.

1_no_code_path_creates_a_user.removed: create_throwaway_user (38 lines), purge_user (14), reconcile_throwaway_users (57), _THROWAWAY_PASSWORD, and the `provisioned` teardown list. Deleted, not flag-gated, so it cannot be re-enabled by accident.
1_no_code_path_creates_a_user.grep: admin/users now appears exactly twice in the harness, both in prose explaining what was removed. Two stale Gap labels that still pointed operators at POST /admin/users ('throwaway second-owner fixture principal') were retired to NO-SECOND-OWNER-PRINCIPAL against /auth/login and /auth/me.
1_no_code_path_creates_a_user.asserted_at_the_transport_not_by_reading: tests/test_rbac_verify_harness.py::test_run_never_creates_or_deletes_a_user records every request a full run makes and fails on any POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE to /admin/users, and separately asserts the user count is unchanged. A future edit that reintroduces provisioning anywhere in the call graph fails there.

2_one_new_name_not_eight.status: RETIRED by PR #343 — the name was deleted along with the cron that needed it
2_one_new_name_not_eight.what_is_true_now: There is no environment variable. RbacVerifier.run() takes supplied_principals as a parameter: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] mapping role -> (email, password) for principals that ALREADY EXIST. Nothing reads the environment and nothing creates a user. The tests pass principals in directly.
2_one_new_name_not_eight.the_lesson: RBAC_VERIFY_PRINCIPALS was invented one commit before being deleted for existing. PR #343: "an environment variable I invented one commit earlier, which is exactly the thing I am supposed not to do." The justification below argued the name carried information nothing else did, and that was true of the name in isolation — but the feature it served was itself unrequested, so the whole branch of reasoning started one step too late.

original_claim.name: RBAC_VERIFY_PRINCIPALS — a single JSON object mapping role -> {email, password}.
original_claim.why_a_new_name_is_justified_here: PR #336 deleted RBAC_VERIFY_USERNAME/PASSWORD because they DUPLICATED AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD and 'added a concept and bought nothing'. This carries information that exists nowhere else — the identities of pre-existing non-owner principals — and deleting it changes behaviour: without it there is no non-owner principal and the role matrix cannot run at all. It is the thing that lets the harness stop provisioning. Stated in the constant's docstring so the next reader does not re-litigate it.

3_absent_principals_abort_loudly.status: RETIRED by PR #343 — there is no process to exit, so there are no exit codes
3_absent_principals_abort_loudly.what_is_true_now: main() is gone. The no-vacuous-pass property it protected is unchanged and still enforced inside the matrix: a missing deny-tier principal records NO-DENY-PRINCIPAL and fails the run, and a missing owner positive records OWNER-POSITIVE-NOT-RUN. An owner-only matrix still cannot pass quietly.

original_claim.behaviour: main() exits 2 (the existing setup-abort code the workflow already renders as a loud ::error) with a named, actionable reason. There is NO fallback to provisioning and NO owner-only mode — an owner-only matrix has no deny tier, so it would pass vacuously and be indistinguishable from a real green run. Malformed JSON, an unknown role, a missing password, a bare username and any @tracelab.local address are each refused with their own message.
original_claim.test: test_main_exits_2_when_principals_are_absent asserts the exit code AND that the message names RBAC_VERIFY_PRINCIPALS — the abort itself, not merely the absence of a crash. Eight more cases in TestResolveVerificationPrincipals.

4_both_deny_tiers_stay_mandatory.behaviour: A partial principal set still runs the matrix rather than refusing to start: member or viewer missing records NO-DENY-PRINCIPAL and fails, and the gap distinguishes "supplied but could not authenticate" from "not supplied at all". Only the supply mechanism changed — principals now arrive as a run() argument instead of parsed JSON from the environment.
4_both_deny_tiers_stay_mandatory.note: The test that pinned this at the CLI boundary (test_partial_set_parses_so_the_run_can_fail_loudly) went with main(). The matrix-level behaviour it described is still covered by the harness suite.

5_next_step_367_closed.status: MET — and the first implementation was wrong in a way only a mutation test caught
5_next_step_367_closed.what_ships: project_owner_read_positive_matrix: a durable project owned by the MEMBER principal (_MEMBER_FIXTURE_PROJECT_NAME, find-or-create, never deleted), a document seeded into it BY THE OWNER, and a 200 assertion for the member reading it.
5_next_step_367_closed.the_mistake_worth_recording: The first version seeded the document as the MEMBER. That makes document.owner_id == the member, so authorize() returns True at the plain owner clause (app/core/authorization.py:143) and the project-owner path below it never executes. The check passed for the wrong reason. A mutation that disabled the project-owner clause outright left it GREEN. Seeding as the owner produces the only shape that reaches the clause under test: a document the member does NOT own, inside a project the member DOES.
5_next_step_367_closed.why_durable_not_per_run: Sprint 55's plan was to create the project and delete it afterwards. That would not have worked: DELETE /projects only soft-deletes (app/api/v1/projects.py:220), so a per-run project strands a dead row on every tick — the same trap the owner fixture already avoids.
5_next_step_367_closed.gated_note_replaced: The Sprint 55 'GATED —' note is gone. Its absence is now a GAP (OWNER-POSITIVE-NOT-RUN), not a note: a deny-only matrix passes just as happily on a system that denies everyone.

7_workflow_note_says_what_is_true.status: RETIRED by PR #343 — the workflow file was deleted outright
7_workflow_note_says_what_is_true.what_is_true_now: .github/workflows/rbac-verify-production.yml no longer exists. There is no schedule, no workflow_dispatch, and no cron slot to restore. RBAC enforcement is checked by the local suite: tests/test_rbac_verify_mutation_proof.py injects a real fail-open regression into authorize() and requires the matrix to catch it, against a TestClient with enforcement on.
7_workflow_note_says_what_is_true.still_worth_knowing: The login-budget finding under findings_from_the_work remains accurate for any future against-production run: five logins against a 5-per-60s limit is zero headroom.

original_claim.schedule: STILL REMOVED, deliberately. The note now says the CAUSE is fixed, names the single remaining precondition (an operator creating the principals once and setting the secret), and gives the exact cron slot to restore — '25 */6 * * *', offset from Production Smoke at ':55' so the two never contend for the login rate limit.
original_claim.credential_check: Now also requires RBAC_VERIFY_PRINCIPALS and prints the JSON shape it expects, so a first-time operator is not guessing.

findings_from_the_work.login_budget_has_zero_headroom: A run performs exactly five logins — owner plus four principals — against a 5-per-60s limit (app/core/rate_limit.py). Discovered because an earlier version of the test fixture minted an owner API key first, which pushed the run's last login to a 429. Unchanged from before this mission (it was five then too), but now recorded in the workflow note: adding a sixth login anywhere breaks the run.
findings_from_the_work.the_local_suite_never_exercised_pedr_sea: RetrievalService returns [] WITHOUT searching when the caller has no accessible projects. Every earlier version of the harness test sailed past the whole vector stack because its throwaway member owned nothing. Giving the member a project it owns made preflight genuinely run and hit three things this machine does not have, in order: an OpenAI key (401 on the placeholder), a Qdrant collection (400), and PostgreSQL full-text syntax that SQLite cannot parse ('unrecognized token: @'). All three are ENVIRONMENT limits, not enforcement findings — production has all three for real. Stubbed at the single shared seam (HybridSearchService.search -> []), which reproduces exactly what the caller saw before while letting the authorization path execute.
